sentences.text: Laopteryx is a pterosaur discovered in the Upper Jurassic Morrison Formation of Wyoming, United States.
The genus was named in 1881 by Othniel Charles Marsh.
The type species of the genus is Laopteryx priscus, also described by Marsh in 1881.
The holotype, which is the specimen the species is based on, is a partial skull designated YPM 1800 found in Quarry 9 at Como Bluff.
A single tooth found near the skull is referred to this type specimen.
In 1986, John Ostrom restudied the fossil and concluded that Laopteryx was a pterosaur.
Ostrom suggested that the single tooth likely belonged to a crocodylomorph.
Laopteryx is regarded as a nomen dubium because its fragmentary remains are not diagnostic enough to classify future fossils.
Another potential Archaeopteryx-type bird, Palaeopteryx, was described from the Upper Jurassic of the US about a century after Laopteryx.
